page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the instance is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 20.0 GB per core. Crucially, it includes a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong capabilities in specialized workloads. The NVIDIA H100 GPU delivers top-tier performance for large language model inference, achieving 10515.12 tokens per second for prompt processing and 547.27 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model. CPU performance is supported by advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions, which facilitate deep learning and vector operations. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression register as strong, while bzip3 single-threaded decompression reaches top-tier levels. Other general CPU and memory benchmarks, such as PassMark CPU and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range.

The qualitative cost profile of this server reflects its high-end GPU and substantial memory capacity. The inclusion of an enterprise-grade NVIDIA H100 GPU with 80 GB VRAM makes it a specialized resource where the primary value resides in accelerator-driven compute density rather than raw CPU core count. However, users should note that the 12 vCPUs are on a shared allocation model, which may introduce performance variability under sustained, non-GPU CPU-bound workloads. Additionally, the complete lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which represents a structural tradeoff for data-intensive pipelines.

This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as deep learning model training, LLM inference, high-performance data science jobs, and parallelized scientific computing. The massive 240 GB system memory and 80 GB VRAM also make it appropriate for memory-intensive AI pipelines and complex simulation tasks.
